title: Id allocation must be worktree-aware and ledger-backed under a common-dir lock (DEC-179 part 1)
description:
DEC-179 part (1), closing measurement (m1): allocation is refs-aware only, so two sessions on two worktrees of one repository that each create before committing both mint N+1, and the merge is an add/add conflict on the same .quest/tasks/

-.json path. Current code: nextTaskId and highestSequenceOnOtherRefs, plus nextDraftId, in src/cli/main.ts; nextPlanningId and highestPlanningSequenceOnOtherRefs cover milestones and decisions. The git common dir is already resolved (src/adapters/workspaces/local-workspaces.ts runs git rev-parse --git-common-dir and keeps commonDirectory), but nothing lists worktrees today. Ruled by opum-doc DEC-179; implement its outcome text exactly. This is part 1 of 4, order (1) then (4) then (2) then (3).

acceptanceCriteria.text: A create, for any id family (task, draft, milestone, decision), allocates its id under an exclusive lock held at <git-common-dir>/quest/alloc.lock.

The candidate id is one above the highest of: every local ref and remote-tracking ref (the current rule); the .quest working tree of every worktree, enumerated by git worktree list --porcelain, including uncommitted records; and the reservation ledger at <common-dir>/quest/reserved-ids.
The allocated id is appended to the reservation ledger before the lock is released.
A ledger entry is pruned once a record carrying that id is visible in any ref or worktree, or once it is older than 7 days.
Allocation performs no network access and no fetch; a stale lock older than 30s whose holder pid is gone is broken, and the run states that it did so.
A .quest directory with no Git repository behind it allocates exactly as today (working-tree-only, unchanged).

Proved both ways: two concurrent creates in two worktrees of one repository get distinct ids; with the lock and ledger disabled the same two concurrent creates collide (the mutation arm); and a create in a non-git directory is unchanged.

The allocator orders ids by their NUMERIC sequence, never by their characters, and a test proves it: ids crossing a digit boundary (9 -> 10 and 99 -> 100) allocate correctly, and the test fails when the comparison is changed to a string sort.

plan: 1. Confirm the numeric-comparator claim in the filing note against src/cli/main.ts, and confirm compareTaskIds is on dev (a28c8182).
2. Add GitPort.listWorktrees (git worktree list --porcelain) and its local-git adapter implementation.
3. New allocation module: common-dir alloc.lock, reservation ledger, per-worktree .quest scan, highest-id selection through compareTaskIds.
4. Rewire nextTaskId, nextDraftId and nextPlanningId through it; keep the non-Git path working-tree-only and unchanged.
5. Tests: two-worktree concurrency green, mutation arm with lock and ledger disabled red, non-git unchanged, 9 to 10 and 99 to 100 digit boundary, stale-lock break reported.
6. Measure the diff against the 400-line ceiling; if it does not fit, stop and report a split before opening the PR.
implementationNotes: Part (1) finding recorded by the filing session: the allocator ALREADY compares the numeric sequence, not string order -- src/cli/main.ts:1339-1342 (highestSequenceOnOtherRefs: Number() then Math.max), :1361-1365 (nextTaskId working-tree scan), :1413-1415 (nextDraftId), :1673-1675 (highestPlanningSequenceOnOtherRefs), :1700-1701 (nextPlanningId). Do not regress this; the added criterion is the missing digit-boundary test, not a comparator change. Existing allocation tests (test/qcli279-refs-aware-task-id-allocation.test.ts, test/qcli290-refs-aware-draft-planning-id-allocation.test.ts) exercise sequences that do not cross 9->10 or 99->100 for the task family.

DEC-181 / team-lead order change: HOLD this task until opum-ai/quest-cli#604 merges (tracked by QCLI-497). Part (1) then builds its numeric comparison ON the compareTaskIds introduced by #604 -- there is no second comparator. The digit-boundary criterion (index 7: 9 -> 10 and 99 -> 100, red under a string sort) still stands.

Dependency on QCLI-497 removed 2026-10-13 (team-lead instruction). QCLI-495 depended on QCLI-497 only to build its numeric id compare on #604 compareTaskIds rather than a second comparator. #604 is squash-merged on dev as a28c8182, so compareTaskIds (src/domain/tasks/tasks.ts) is available; #605 and #606 still pending under QCLI-497 do not change it and are not prerequisites for part (1).

STOPPED BEFORE THE PR: the change does not fit the ~400-line ceiling, and it retires the input one existing test constructs. Branch feat/QCLI-495-worktree-aware-id-allocation, nothing pushed.

MEASURED SIZE: 873 insertions / 105 deletions across 5 files = 978 changed lines. New src/application/tasks/id-allocation.ts is 394 lines (251 code, 119 comment, 24 blank) and carries lock acquisition, the 30s/dead-pid stale break, the ledger read/append/prune, and the two per-worktree record scans. The four-family rewiring is 185/105 in src/cli/main.ts. The new test file is 268 lines.

STATE: all 8 acceptance criteria are implemented and verified; lint (its 8 warnings are all pre-existing, in other files), format:check, typecheck and layer:check are clean. New suite test/qcli495-worktree-aware-id-allocation.test.ts: 6 tests, 6 pass. Full suite 1176 pass / 1 fail. Both mutation arms reproduced: changing the allocator one comparison (sort(compareTaskIds)) to a bare sort() turns the 9->10 / 99->100 test red (exit 5); disabling the lock and ledger turns the two-worktree concurrency test red 3 runs of 3 (exit 5, task_already_exists) -- DEC-179 m1 reproduced against the fix.

THE REGRESSION IS THE INTENDED EFFECT: test/qcli425-conflict-cause-and-echo.test.ts "a writer race stays distinguishable" builds its input as 16 concurrent auto-allocating task create in ONE worktree and asserts that some of them FAIL with the concurrent-change wording and no sentRevision. QCLI-495 removes exactly that race. Pre-fix control (stash, same invocation) 3 runs of 3 GREEN; post-fix 4 runs of 4 RED. The contract that test asserts is still live but now reachable only through an explicit --id writer racing an auto-allocating one, which is not deterministically constructible. So the PR cannot go green without a decision on that test.

OPTION A (recommended): one PR at 978 changed lines, with the size stated in the PR body. DEC-179 part (1) is a single outcome paragraph naming all four families and every acceptance criterion is in this task, so splitting means rewriting this task acceptance criteria and a ratified decision scope -- team-lead and opum-doc authority, not mine. Mitigation: three commits (module+port, wiring, tests) so the reviewer reads the mechanism before the wiring. The 400 figure is the skill own "roughly ... past that the reviewer skims" heuristic, not a gate.

OPTION B: split along the mechanism/proof seam -- 495a the port + module + four-family wiring + non-git path (about 605 changed lines), 495b the proof suite (about 373). It separates a change from its proof, which the fleet rules forbid, and neither half is comfortably under 400. Splitting by family breadth instead (task+draft, then milestone+decision) barely helps: the module is shared, so the larger half stays about 700.

QCLI-425 TEST, needs its own answer either way: (i, recommended) rewrite that one test to assert the invariant the change creates -- the same 16 concurrent creates in one worktree now all succeed with distinct ids, which is QCLI-495 at higher concurrency -- keeping the concurrent-wording contract on the arms that still reach it; or (ii) retire it and file a follow-up to re-cover the wording. (i) and Option A are what I would do next absent an answer.

PAUSED BY TEAM-LEAD 2026-10-13 for the paired lore+quest v0.13.1 release cut (constitution Article 3; DEC-182, a sonnet session). No PR opened. Resumes after the release, with this note as its brief.

MEASUREMENTS: 873 insertions / 105 deletions across 5 files = 978 changed lines. src/application/tasks/id-allocation.ts 394 lines (251 code, 119 comment, 24 blank); src/cli/main.ts 185/105; test/qcli495-worktree-aware-id-allocation.test.ts 268 lines; src/ports/git.ts 12; src/adapters/git/local-git.ts 14.

EVIDENCE: lint (its 8 warnings are all pre-existing in other files), format:check, typecheck and layer:check clean. New suite 6 tests, 6 pass. Full suite 1176 pass / 1 fail. Mutation arm 1: the allocator one comparison (sort(compareTaskIds)) replaced by a bare .sort() turns the 9->10 / 99->100 test RED, exit 5 (id already taken). Mutation arm 2: lock and ledger disabled turns the two-worktree concurrency test RED 3 runs of 3, exit 5, task_already_exists -- DEC-179 m1 reproduced against the fix. Both arms reverted; no MUTATION residue remains in src/ or test/.

TEAM-LEAD RULINGS, 2026-10-13: Q1 = Option A -- ONE PR, size stated and justified in the body, three reviewable commits (module+port, wiring, tests). Q2 = Option (i) -- rewrite the QCLI-425 race test to assert the new invariant (16 concurrent creates in one worktree all succeed with distinct ids) and keep the concurrent-change wording covered deterministically.

WHAT IS LEFT, in order:
1. Q2(i), applied AFTER the release. Not started: the QCLI-425 suite is process-spawning only -- no adapter stub and no barrier seam exists -- and no other arm in that file reaches the concurrent wording, so the deterministic half needs a seam that does not exist today. Ruling offers the fallback: keep the wording assertion on whatever arms still reach it and record the uncovered path in the PR body and on QCLI-425.
2. Open ONE PR into dev at 978 changed lines with the size justification, then let the required checks run on the exact head. The suite is RED on test/qcli425-conflict-cause-and-echo.test.ts until step 1 lands: pre-fix control (stash to dev, same invocation) 3 runs of 3 GREEN, post-fix 4 runs of 4 RED at expect(failures.length).toBeGreaterThan(0) receiving 0. That failure is the intended effect of this task, not a defect in it.
3. Check all 8 acceptance criteria with the evidence above and complete the task in that same PR.

RESUMED 2026-10-20 (leader plan word, opum-doc 20:05Z). The pushed branch had no PR and was 32 commits behind dev; merged origin/dev into it (no rebase of a pushed branch), clean. Added: the question family (Q-N, QCLI-445, after the criteria) through the same allocator with its own two-worktree test (red 3 of 3 with the lock bypassed); the QCLI-425 race test rewritten per the 2026-10-13 ruling Q2(i); a 7-day ledger expiry test (red when the TTL is changed to 700 days) and a no-network test (GIT_TRACE to a file, remote configured but unreachable, trace read and non-empty). FINDING: with allocation fixed, 16 concurrent creates in one worktree can still lose the tracker revision check: 1 writer in 1 of 12 runs lost, exit 5, concurrent wording. A conflict, not a collision. Baseline with lock and ledger bypassed: 4 to 7 of 16 win; with the fix 15 or 16. The rewritten test asserts at least 14 win with distinct ids and any loser keeps the QCLI-425 wording; the wording keeps a deterministic arm in racing edits (4 runs of 4 lost 7 to 12 of 16). PR: opum-ai/quest-cli#646. Local gate on bun 1.3.14 (pin 1.4.2): 1244 pass, 1 fail, the QCLI-411 pinned-runtime check. Lint 8 warnings, all pre-existing.
finalSummary: Every id family (task, draft, milestone, decision, and question) now allocates under an exclusive lock at <git-common-dir>/quest/alloc.lock. The candidate id is one above the highest across every ref, every worktree .quest (git worktree list --porcelain, uncommitted included) and the reservation ledger <common-dir>/quest/reserved-ids; the id is appended to the ledger before the lock is released; entries drop once the record is visible or after 7 days; no fetch or network is used; a stale lock (over 30s, holder pid gone) is broken and the run says so; a .quest with no Git repository allocates as before; ordering is numeric through compareTaskIds. Verified by test/qcli495-worktree-aware-id-allocation.test.ts (9 tests, 9 pass): two worktrees creating before either commits get distinct ids for every family; with the lock and ledger bypassed the same creates collide (red 3 of 3), a bare string sort turns the 9 to 10 and 99 to 100 test red, and changing the TTL to 700 days turns the expiry test red. The QCLI-425 race test was rewritten because QCLI-495 removes the collision it constructed. Delivered in opum-ai/quest-cli#646; the run that validated it is cited in the PR, and the full local gate read 1244 pass with only the QCLI-411 pinned-runtime check failing on bun 1.3.14.
